body: I'd like to discuss https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/11981 again - @noamr has approved but I would like to get another look from @annevk.
https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11542 has an Agenda+ already, requesting that attendees take a look if possible so that we can have a meaningful discussion! 😊
We'd like to discuss #11641, checking if there're any updates from @annevk on the review needed to proceed to stage 2.
I'd like to give a very quick update on revisions and progress on the Canvas [writingMode and textOrientation attributes proposal #11449](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11449).

Notes:

- Streaming Content with Declarative Markers: The meeting continued the discussion on the streaming issue (#11542), specifically focusing on out-of-order streaming using a declarative approach. Noam Rosenthal proposed using magical marker comments for updating content, which allows the same HTML stream to update an element multiple times, such as appending search results. Noam suggested using markers only, which could either replace the content between a start and end marker or just replace the marker itself if neither a start nor an end is present. The proposed markers would be in the serialized markup, manually added by an author or CMS. Jake Archibald clarified that if a marker's start and end span an unbalanced tree, the implicit end would be the end of the parent element's sibling list. Simon Pieters raised concerns about giving power to comments, suggesting this might be a safety concern, and proposed that if processing instructions are desired, they should be parsed as actual processing instruction nodes.  Kurt Catti-Schmidt inquired about the scope of marker names, and Noam confirmed they would be in the tree scope and the scope of the template's parent. Stephen Chenney raised a point about indicating that content is expected to appear for accessibility, though Noam noted that HTML already provides ways for this, such as using `loading` attributes. Noam mentioned an earlier alternative using element-based methods (like `append` or `replace` children) instead of markers, which was considered less flexible and more verbose. Olli Pettay and Anne van Kesteren preferred the marker approach, believing it offered more flexibility for use cases like infinite scrolling and DOM parts. Conversely, Jake preferred the element-based approach, citing concerns that minifiers might remove the marker logic. Robert Flack supported markers, arguing that the element-based approach imposes structure on the DOM irrelevant to semantics. Mike Smith mentioned that static analysis and checkers, like the W3C validator, are typically designed for elements and attributes, suggesting the element-based approach might be easier for error checking. Noam countered that the ecosystem, particularly frameworks like React and Marco, already use comment nodes for out-of-order streaming to avoid intermediate elements. Jake's testing showed popular HTML minifiers do not remove processing instructions by default, although they might remove comments. Simon raised sanitizers as a potential obstacle for adopting PI or comment syntax, as they might strip out comments or not be configured for the new syntax. Noam agreed to further develop the processing instruction concept and seek views from Mozilla folks.
- Focus Group (#11641) Stage Two Review Jacques Newman provided an update on the "focus group" proposal (11641), noting that the TAG had given a thumbs-up. Jacques sought further review, especially from Mozilla. Anne indicated Apple had no concrete feedback yet. Olli mentioned that while the proposal generally looks good, the event handling model is currently too vague for a compatible implementation, and Jacques agreed it could use some expansion.
- HTML Canvas Text Writing Mode Support (#11449) Stephen Chenney presented the proposal to add `writing-mode` and `text-orientation` support to HTML canvas text, limiting it to horizontal and vertical modes since sideways is trivial in canvas. Stephen expected to submit a spec PR in about a week and requested feedback from Apple and Mozilla.
- Module Preload for Style and JSON PR (#11981) Kurt Catti-Schmidt addressed a pull request for module preload for style and JSON, seeking clarity on conformance. Anne recommended redefining "preload destination" in HTML to a short list of allowed values, consistent with Noam's suggestion, and defining a separate module preload destination.
- Event Firing for Commands (https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12021) Jake Archibald raised a point about inconsistent specification wording regarding events fired on commands, especially for `popover`. The current browser behavior suggests that all elements can have popover commands, even without the `popover` attribute. The discussion leaned toward an element-by-element approach where a command is only fired if the element supports it, though `popover` and `scroll` commands would work on a broader range of elements. This approach supports feature detection for developers, as noted by Keith Cirkel.
